taxonomy.note: Current Kew/POWO accepts the spelling Andropogon gerardi Vitman. Many North American sources, including ITIS/NPSOT, use Andropogon gerardii; preserve that familiar spelling as an alias/search term.

evidence: Hays — City/Austin-area management documentation for the Hays County Ranch tract lists big bluestem as a native tallgrass component.
Travis — Texas Conservation Action Plan Blackland Prairie community documentation explicitly includes Andropogon gerardii in Travis County.
Williamson — NPSOT Williamson County documents locally sourced big bluestem seed from historic MoKan Prairie.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Do not infer county occurrence from statewide/ecoregional range.

morphology.look_here_first: Look at the top first: big bluestem usually has 2–6 fingerlike racemes radiating together, often forming the classic 'turkey foot.' It is a tall robust prairie grass, not a fluffy plume.
diagnostic_traits: tall perennial bunchgrass, commonly well over 1 m
2–6 digitate racemes at the culm tip
turkey-foot silhouette when 3 principal racemes are developed
leaf blades roughly 5–10 mm wide in GrassBase
racemes not enclosed in inflated sheaths
overall inflorescence open-fingered rather than woolly or broomlike

confusers.separator: Bushy bluestem forms dense fluffy silvery clusters partly emerging from upper sheaths rather than a clean turkey-foot of fingerlike racemes.
Broomsedge has narrow racemes partly enclosed by conspicuous spathe-like sheaths and abundant silky hairs; it lacks the big digitate turkey-foot head.

installation_guardrail: Strict PASS complete; install under standing blanket approval.
